title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for 'Galois theory of motives' (1965). Grothendieck is setting up the linear-algebraic machinery needed for categories of motives with coefficients and for changing the coefficient ring.

Definition. Fix a commutative ring A. A 'catégorie de D… sur A' is a pseudo-abelian (Karoubian) A-linear category C for which there is an A-algebra O and an A-linear equivalence C ≃ P(O/A). Here P(O/A) is the category of (right) O-modules that are projective and locally free of finite type over Spec A. The eponym is hard to read; the image suggests 'Deuring' rather than 'Demazure'. O is presumably finite locally free over A, typically Azumaya or separable.

Characterisation (Morita recognition). C is of this type if and only if there is an object X0 with O = End_C(X0) such that:
- (a) for every P in P(O/A) the 'tensor' P ⊗_O X0 exists in C. It is defined by representability; it exists automatically when P is a direct summand of O^n, given finite sums and Karoubianness.
- (b) the functor P ↦ P ⊗_O X0 is an equivalence P(O/A) → C.
He then asserts this holds for every X0.

NB (Morita invariance). Up to non-unique equivalence, C is determined by O. The algebras O and O' give equivalent categories if and only if O' ≃ End_O(P) for some P in P(O/A). In other words, O' is obtained from O by 'twisting by inner automorphisms via P', which is the Morita-equivalence / Brauer-class viewpoint. In the commutative case one gets O ≃ O', since the centre is a Morita invariant.

Exercise (beginning of a base-change formalism). Let u: A → A' be a ring map, C an A-linear category of the above type and C' an A'-linear category. A functor F: C → C' is called admissible (relative to u) if:
- it is A-linear, and
- it commutes with the operations P ⊗_O X, for X in C, O ⊂ End_C(X) a subalgebra, and P in P(O/A).
The page breaks off at 'Il suffit…'. Presumably the continuation says it suffices to check this for one generating X0. It would then construct the scalar extension C ⊗_A A' ≃ P(O⊗_A A'/A') as the universal recipient of admissible functors.

This is the precursor of 'extension of scalars of the coefficient ring' for motives (motives with coefficients in a number field E, base change E → E'). Saavedra and Deligne later formalised it as C ⊗_k k' and X ⊗ M.
errors: The claim 'for all X0 in C, a) and b) hold' is false as stated. X0 = 0 fails, and more generally X0 must be a progenerator: a generator, i.e. of everywhere positive rank / faithful. It is correct only under hypotheses such as O Azumaya, Spec A connected and X0 nonzero at every point.
Likewise, 'O and O' give equivalent C iff O' ≃ End(P) for some P in P(O/A)' requires P to be a progenerator. Counterexample: O = A×A, P = A×0 gives End(P) = A, which is not Morita equivalent to A×A.
The description 'obtained by twisting by inner automorphisms' is accurate only locally, e.g. for Azumaya algebras, where O' is a twisted form; in general Morita equivalence is not a twist.
Minor point: the existence of P ⊗_O X0 is automatic in a pseudo-abelian additive category for finitely generated projective P, so condition (a) is redundant under the standing hypotheses.

ideas.what: Recognition of a Karoubian A-linear category as finitely generated projective modules over the endomorphism algebra of a generating object
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; similar formalism in Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972), which follows Grothendieck's program

ideas.what: Morita invariance; equivalence classes of such categories correspond to algebras up to O' = End_O(P); commutative O is recovered from the category
ideas.modern_name: Morita equivalence, Brauer-class viewpoint, centre as Morita invariant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Morita; Bass; Auslander–Goldman (Azumaya, Brauer group over rings, 1960)
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I–III (1966–68) uses Azumaya algebras and twisted forms; the Morita formalism appears implicitly

ideas.what: Admissible functors relative to A → A', commuting with the action X ↦ P ⊗_O X, as the basis for extension of scalars of linear categories
ideas.modern_name: Extension of scalars of linear / Tannakian categories (C ⊗_A A'); tensoring an object by a module over its endomorphisms
ideas.where_published: Not published by Grothendieck; the formalism appears in Saavedra's thesis and Deligne's work

missed.claim: The page starts a universal-property definition of base change for Morita-type linear categories, via admissible functors commuting with P ⊗_O X, in the service of changing coefficient rings for motives in 1965. It breaks off. This is an early, pre-Saavedra trace of the coefficient-extension formalism. Mathematically it is subsumed by later work (Saavedra 1972; Deligne 1990), so it is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: Un foncteur F : C → C' est dit admissible (pour u) s'il est A-linéaire, et s'il commute à l'opération P ⊗_O X ... Il suffit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck's 1965 motive notes already contained the scalar-extension machinery later credited to Saavedra and Deligne. It is relevant for history and for motives with coefficients, but there is no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Morita theory written out as preparatory material for motives with coefficients. The only point of interest is the early (1965) appearance of an admissible-functor approach to extension of scalars, which was later formalised by Saavedra and Deligne.
transcription_corrections: Title eponym: the handwriting reads more like 'Deuring' (or similar) than 'Demazure'; uncertain.
Under P(O/A): likely 'modules à droite sur O, loc. libres de type fini sur Spec A' rather than 'projectifs de type fini … de rang 1'.
In the exercise: 'O ⊂ End_C(X)' (a subalgebra) rather than 'O ∈ End_C(X)'.
The parenthetical after 'Si O est commutatif' is hard to read; 'ou inversement !' is doubtful.
